pages.name: Quick Start
pages.content:
Using Scene Grid Presets

Scene Grid Presets give GMs four ready-made scales, each available as either a flat-top hex grid or a square grid. Both shapes use the same real-world distance per grid space and record the same rules mode for Scene-aware automation.

Set the Default for New Scenes

  1. Open Game Settings → Configure Settings → System Settings.
  2. Find Default Scene Grid.
  3. Choose the Close Quarters, Battle, City, or Travel scale and the preferred grid shape, or choose System Manifest Default.
  4. Save the settings.

Apply a Preset to One Scene

  1. Right-click the Scene in the navigation bar or Scenes directory and choose Configure.
  2. Open the Grid tab.
  3. Find the GM-only Grid Presets panel.
  4. Click the required hex or square preset button.

Clicking a preset saves an existing Scene immediately. When configuring a Scene that has not yet been created, finish by saving the Scene.

What a Preset Does

A preset changes the grid type, distance, and units. It deliberately preserves the grid's pixel size, offsets, and map dimensions, so the GM must still align the grid to the artwork.

Terrain Regions

Grid presets do not classify map terrain. Enable the optional tactical assistance and add Tactical Terrain Region behaviors separately when the Scene should supply movement, cover, infiltration, visibility, and ranged-attack assistance.

pages.name: World Default
pages.content:
World Default

Default Scene Grid is a world-level GM setting. It supplies a starting grid for genuinely new Scenes created in the world.

Available Choices

Each of these four scales is available as Flat-Top Hexes or Squares:

  • Close Quarters — 2.5 m: the system default is the hex version; both versions suit rooms and detailed interiors.
  • Battle — 10 m: tactical outdoor encounters.
  • City — 200 m: movement and travel through built-up areas.
  • Travel — 10 km: regional and overland travel.
  • System Manifest Default: leaves Foundry's core grid values untouched when the Scene is created.

What Is Not Changed

The setting does not alter existing Scenes. Scenes imported from JSON or a compendium retain their source configuration, including their grid and stored rules mode. Apply a preset from the Scene's Grid tab when an imported or existing Scene should use one of these modes.

The chosen default also establishes the initial Scene rules mode. A new Close Quarters Scene starts with urban rules enabled regardless of grid shape; the other three scales start without that toggle.

pages.name: Applying a Preset to a Scene
pages.content:
Applying a Preset to a Scene

  1. Open Scene Configuration.
  2. Select the Grid tab.
  3. Under Grid Presets, choose the required scale and click its Hex or Square button.
  4. For a newly prepared Scene, save the configuration. An existing Scene is saved as soon as the button is clicked.
  5. Use Foundry's normal grid tools to adjust pixel size and offset until the virtual grid matches the map.

Preset Side Effects

  • Applying either Close Quarters shape enables urban rules for the Scene.
  • Applying either Battle, City, or Travel shape clears the Scene's explicit urban toggle.
  • Changing between hex and square versions retains the corresponding scale's automation mode.
  • No preset changes Enable confined-space hazards on this Scene.
  • The background image, dimensions, grid pixel size, and alignment offsets are preserved.

Changing Rules Mode Later

Use a preset button whenever the Scene should change from one rules mode or grid shape to another. Manually changing only the displayed distance or units does not replace a rules mode that was explicitly recorded by an earlier preset.

pages.name: Preset Reference
pages.content:
Preset Reference

ScaleDistance per Grid SpaceShapesTypical Use
Close Quarters2.5 mHex or SquareRooms, buildings, tunnels, and detailed sector maps. This is an approximate scale for artwork that may not have been designed around a measured grid.
Battle10 mHex or SquareTactical outdoor combat and larger sites.
City200 mHex or SquareUrban movement, city travel stretches, and district-scale maps.
Travel10 kmHex or SquareRegional and overland travel maps.

Grid Shape

The Hex choices use Foundry's flat-top, odd-column offset grid. If a map image uses the opposite column offset, select Foundry's alternative flat-top even-column Grid Type after applying the preset. The Square choices use Foundry's standard square grid. Grid shape does not change the selected scale or automation mode.

Measurement

The distance is the real-world distance represented by one grid space. A token that moves three Battle spaces therefore moves 30 m; three City spaces represent 600 m; and three Travel spaces represent 30 km.

pages.name: Urban and Confined-Space Rules
pages.content:
Urban and Confined-Space Rules

The Grid Presets panel also contains two independent Scene rule controls.

Urban Rules

Enable Urban Operations rules on this Scene makes the broader urban action set and supporting automation available on a Scene of any scale. Close Quarters always behaves as an urban Scene, even if its displayed checkbox is later cleared, and additionally enables its close-quarters-only sector actions, engagement rules, blind fire, and indoor handling.

Applying Close Quarters turns the urban toggle on. Applying Battle, City, or Travel turns the explicit toggle off, so re-enable it afterward when a non-Close-Quarters Scene also needs urban rules.

Confined-Space Hazards

Enable confined-space hazards on this Scene activates the Scene-wide confined environment used by supported blast, ricochet, structural-collapse, and debris workflows. It is independent of both scale and urban rules.

A Close Quarters preset does not enable confined-space hazards automatically. Turn the setting on only for underground, enclosed, or otherwise hazardous areas where those effects belong. Applying another grid preset does not clear it.

pages.name: City and Travel Integration
pages.content:
City and Travel Integration

City Preset

When a City Scene is active, a Travel Party automatically uses its urban travel interface unless Water Travel is enabled on that Party. Urban travel divides play into short stretches and provides March, Drive, Keep Watch, and Other assignments together with the city movement, fuel, and GM stretch tools.

Both City grid shapes supply the expected 200 m measurement and record City mode. The active Scene determines the automatic integration, so activate the appropriate Scene before managing the Travel Party.

Travel Preset

Both Travel grid shapes supply 10 km spaces for regional movement. They do not automatically select Water Travel or another specialised Travel Party mode. The Party continues to use its standard travel workflow unless a GM enables a different mode on its sheet.

Other Presets

Battle and Close Quarters Scenes do not automatically select a special Travel Party interface. Use them for encounter movement and Scene-aware combat actions rather than overland progress.

Map Choice

A City or Travel map does not have to contain a printed grid. Set a suitable pixel size for readable tokens and use Foundry's measurement tools with the preset distance. If the artwork does contain squares or hexes, choose the matching shape and calibrate the pixel grid and offsets.

pages.name: Map Alignment and Calibration
pages.content:
Map Alignment and Calibration

A preset provides game scale and grid shape, not image calibration. It preserves the Scene's existing pixel grid size, offsets, background image, and dimensions.

Aligning a Gridded Map

  1. Apply the desired hex or square preset first.
  2. Use Foundry's Grid Configuration tools to make one virtual grid space the same pixel size as one printed map space.
  3. Adjust the horizontal and vertical offsets until the grid lines align.
  4. For a hex map whose alternating columns lean the wrong way, choose the alternative flat-top even-column Grid Type.
  5. Save and test measurement between several distant spaces.

Gridless Artwork

For artwork without a printed grid, choose a pixel size that keeps tokens and labels usable. The preset's distance remains authoritative even though there is no image grid to match.

Keep Mode and Calibration Separate

Use preset buttons to change Scene rules mode, shape, and distance. Use pixel size, offsets, and—when applicable—the equivalent flat-top offset type to fit the artwork. If the distance or shape is edited manually after a preset, the stored rules mode still takes precedence for automation.

Imported Scenes

Imported Scenes preserve their original grid. Inspect the scale and shape before play, apply the intended preset if needed, and then recalibrate the artwork rather than assuming the world default was applied.

pages.name: Prototype Token Sizes and Troubleshooting
pages.content:
Prototype Token Sizes

Grid scale and token footprint are configured separately. Open Game Settings → Configure Settings → System Settings → Default Prototype Token Sizes → Configure Token Sizes to set the default width and height for newly created Characters, NPCs, Vehicles, Units, Parties, and Containers.

  • All Actor types default to 1 × 1 grid space.
  • Width and height may be set independently from 0.25 to 10 grid spaces.
  • Rectangular footprints are useful for vehicles, large storage, and unusual units.
  • The same 1 × 1 token occupies one grid space at every preset; only the shape and real-world distance represented by that space change.
  • The setting affects only genuinely new Actors. Imported Actors, existing prototype tokens, and tokens already placed on a Scene are never resized.

Troubleshooting

The Scale or Shape Is Wrong

Check Grid Type, Distance, and Units, then click the intended preset again. Do not rely on manually editing the grid when automation should also change modes.

The Rules Do Not Match the Displayed Distance

An explicitly stored Scene mode takes precedence over scale inference. Reapply the correct preset.

The Map Art Does Not Align

Adjust pixel grid size and horizontal or vertical offset. Distance controls measurement and will not align the artwork.

Urban or Confined Rules Are Unexpected

Review both Scene toggles. Close Quarters always counts as urban; confined-space hazards remain independent and persist when another preset is applied.

An Existing Token Has the Wrong Size

Edit that Actor's Prototype Token or the placed token directly. The world default is intentionally limited to new Actors.
